correctness.rationale: All radii are angles on the unit sphere. The 12 regular spherical pentagonal Voronoi cells have central inradius rho, terminal radius R, and five disjoint outside-of-side sectors until R. Integrating cap intersections per cell yields the entire CDF without unstated coverage overlaps. The segment derivative is 2 sin(t) alpha(t), yielding the 3/2 onset and quadratic terminal tail by explicit expansions; the surface Green identity gives the mean nearest squared chord loss with exact side length ell. The standalone standard-library checker reproduces the angular cell integrals independently at 21 radii, four threshold tests, 100000 direct samples, and the exact mean via angular quadrature. Finite checks are only corroboration; the analytical argument establishes the continuum identity.

evidence: Fowler et al. (2002, §3(a)) explicitly credits older geometry for the regular icosahedron being an optimal packing and covering and an intermediate twelve-cap solution.
Hardin–Michaels–Saff (2016) defines Voronoi cells and studies separation, covering radius, and icosahedral mesh constructions; it is not a distributional nearest-angle inversion.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing global optimal placement statements dominate any new assertion that the icosahedron is a packing or covering optimizer; that assertion is excluded here. These broader bounds do not specify the exact fraction covered at every intermediate radius, the coefficients of its two threshold asymptotics, or the mean squared-chord loss. No average-loss optimum is asserted.

The 2002 source contains the same coverage observable and known optimal icosahedral placement but reports only packing/covering endpoints for this case; the 2012 source establishes the cap-segment primitive, which is acknowledged and is not claimed new. value.rationale: A globally classical 12-site spherical packing/covering benchmark previously had explicit endpoint angles but no located exact interior CDF. The full coverage curve is the natural distribution of worst-and-average location-to-site error for this canonical geodesic code, and its two distinct sharp threshold powers quantify precisely the first overlap and final uncovered-area exhaustion. The exact average squared chord loss is a nontrivial quantization statistic obtained independently from Voronoi boundary geometry. This is one coherent distribution-and-moment result on a naturally optimal configuration, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or restatement of the one-cap segment primitive.
